visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a graphic animation background featuring a blue gradient and stylized clouds. Large blue and yellow text appears in the center, accompanied by an emoji. The visual style is that of a social media variety show clip. (2) Inside a cluttered bedroom with a wooden bed and a white dresser, a man in a teal t-shirt is drying his hair with a yellow hairdryer. A woman in a white t-shirt sits on the bed looking at her phone. She repeatedly gestures towards him with a frustrated expression, moving her mouth as if calling out. The man eventually stops and looks at her with an annoyed facial expression. (3) Another graphic transition occurs with the same blue gradient background. A different set of large stylized text in Chinese and English appears in the center, indicating a change in the scenario or topic. (4) The setting remains the bedroom. The woman now has a pink towel wrapped around her head and is talking to the man. The man is sitting on the bed, leaning against the headboard and focused on his smartphone. The woman suddenly tosses the yellow hairdryer onto the bed and covers herself with the duvet in a quick, frustrated motion. (5) A third graphic title card appears with a blue background and yellow border. The text is centered and clearly legible, signaling the start of the final segment of the video's list-style structure. (6) Two people are sitting on a bed against a wall covered with colorful posters. A woman in a pink top holds her phone horizontally. A man in a dark green t-shirt is also holding his phone but is turned towards her, shouting with wide eyes and exaggerated hand gestures. His face shows intense anger and disappointment as he points at the screen.

He dominates the mix, while a female voice offers short, quieter responses.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: List-based: Scenario A -> Scenario B -> Scenario C
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video uses a humorous, list-based approach to contrast the behaviors of couples in a 'flat period' of their relationship. By exaggerating everyday conflicts—like ignoring a partner due to a hairdryer, refusing to help with hair drying, or getting angry during a mobile game—it aims to entertain the audience while providing relatable relationship commentary.
